items.note: 225 年诸葛亮南征，“五月渡泸，深入不毛”。

e.note: On his southern campaign in 225 Zhuge Liang "crossed the Lu in the 5th month and went deep into the barren lands".

items.note: 三国时代南北对峙的天堑，魏曹丕临江而叹“固天所以限南北也”。赤壁、夷陵、濡须诸战都发生在江上或江边。

e.note: The natural moat between north and south in the Three Kingdoms; Cao Pi of Wei, looking out over it, sighed that "Heaven surely set it here to divide north from south". Red Cliffs, Yiling, Ruxu and other battles were all fought on or beside the river.

items.note: 238 年司马懿渡辽水，佯攻辽隧，直趋襄平。

e.note: In 238 Sima Yi crossed the Liao River, feinted at Liaosui and made straight for Xiangping.

items.note: 上游流经汉中，中游流经襄阳、樊城，至夏口入江。219 年秋霖雨，汉水暴涨，关羽水淹于禁七军。

e.note: Its upper course runs through Hanzhong and its middle course past Xiangyang and Fancheng, entering the Yangtze at Xiakou. In the autumn rains of 219 the Han River flooded, and Guan Yu drowned Yu Jin's seven armies.

items.note: 215 年孙刘以湘水为界中分荆州。

e.note: In 215 Sun Quan and Liu Bei divided Jing Province between them along the Xiang River.

items.note: 魏吴之间的缓冲地带，魏在淮南、淮北大兴屯田，淮南三叛都发生在淮水南岸的寿春。

e.note: The buffer zone between Wei and Wu; Wei set up military farms on a large scale south and north of the Huai, and the three rebellions in Huainan all took place at Shouchun on its southern bank.

items.note: 上游称故道水，陈仓道沿其河谷而行。

e.note: Its upper course was called the Gudao River, and the Chencang Road followed its valley.

items.note: 东汉初王景治河后，河道自荥阳东北经濮阳、东阿至千乘入海，此后数百年较为安定。黄河是官渡之战两军隔河相持的天然界线，白马、延津、黎阳皆为河上渡口。

e.note: After Wang Jing's river works early in the Eastern Han, the Yellow River ran northeast from Xingyang past Puyang and Dong'e to the sea at Qiansheng, and stayed fairly stable for centuries. In the Guandu campaign it was the natural line across which the two armies faced each other; Baima, Yanjin and Liyang were all crossings on the river.

items.note: 关中的命脉。211 年曹操夜渡渭水筑沙城；234 年诸葛亮屯五丈原，与司马懿隔渭相持。

e.note: The lifeline of Guanzhong. In 211 Cao Cao crossed the Wei by night and built a sand fort; in 234 Zhuge Liang camped at the Wuzhang Plains and faced Sima Yi across the Wei.

items.note: 流经邺城北。204 年曹操引漳水灌邺城。

e.note: It flowed past the north of Ye. In 204 Cao Cao diverted the Zhang to flood Ye.

items.mod: 古济水（今黄河下游大部即其故道）
items.note: 四渎之一，自荥阳分河东流，经定陶、巨野泽东北入海。

e.mod: old Ji River (much of the lower Yellow River now follows its course)
e.note: One of the Four Great Rivers; it left the Yellow River at Xingyang, flowed east past Dingtao and the Juye Marsh, and then northeast to the sea.

items.note: 198 年曹操决沂、泗灌下邳城。

e.note: In 198 Cao Cao broke the banks of the Yi and Si to flood Xiapi.

items.note: 公孙瓒依易水筑易京。

e.note: Gongsun Zan built Yijing beside the Yi River.

items.note: 流经宛城、新野入汉水。197 年张绣反攻宛城，曹操败退至淯水。

e.note: It flowed past Wan and Xinye into the Han River. In 197, when Zhang Xiu turned on Cao Cao at Wan, Cao Cao fell back to the Yu River.

items.note: 196 年孙策渡浙江破王朗。

e.note: In 196 Sun Ce crossed the Zhe River and defeated Wang Lang.

items.note: 255 年姜维于洮西大破魏雍州刺史王经。

e.note: In 255 Jiang Wei routed Wang Jing, the Wei Inspector of Yong Province, at Taoxi.

items.note: 濡须水自巢湖东南流入江，吴于水口筑濡须坞、东兴堤。

e.note: The Ruxu River flows southeast from Chao Lake into the Yangtze; Wu built Ruxu Fort and the Dongxing dyke at its mouth.

items.mod: 内蒙古额济纳（今居延海）

e.mod: Ejin Banner, Inner Mongolia (today's Juyan Lake)

items.note: 魏正始年间邓艾在淮北屯田时修筑的陂塘之一。

e.mod: west of Hongze District, Huai'an, Jiangsu
e.note: One of the reservoirs Deng Ai built while setting up military farms north of the Huai in Wei's Zhengshi era.

items.note: 江汉之间的大片湖沼，汉末已渐萎缩。曹操赤壁战败后经华容道北撤，“道路泥泞”，即行于此。

e.note: A vast expanse of lakes and marshes between the Yangtze and the Han, already shrinking by the late Han. When Cao Cao retreated north along the Huarong Road after Red Cliffs, "the road was deep in mud": his route ran through here.

items.mod: 河北巨鹿、邢台任泽区一带（已淤废）

e.mod: Julu and Renze District area, Xingtai, Hebei (silted up)

items.note: 春秋楚孙叔敖所修，汉末扬州刺史刘馥重修，魏在淮南屯田多赖其灌溉；241 年吴将全琮北伐，决芍陂。

e.mod: south of Shou County, Anhui (Anfeng Pond)
e.note: Built by Sunshu Ao of Chu in the Spring and Autumn period and restored by Liu Fu, Inspector of Yang Province, in the late Han; Wei's military farms in Huainan depended on it for irrigation. In 241 the Wu general Quan Cong attacked north and breached Quebei.

items.note: 流经曹操故里谯县，曹丕南征多自谯沿涡水入淮。

e.note: It flowed past Qiao, Cao Cao's home county; on his southern campaigns Cao Pi often went from Qiao down the Guo into the Huai.

items.note: 198 年曹操决沂、泗灌下邳。

e.note: In 198 Cao Cao broke the banks of the Yi and Si to flood Xiapi.

items.note: 巢湖东出入江的水道，孙吴于水口立濡须坞、筑东兴堤，是魏吴必争的江北要地。

e.note: The waterway leading east from Chao Lake to the Yangtze. Sun Wu set up Ruxu Fort and built the Dongxing dyke at its mouth; it was a key point north of the river that Wei and Wu fought over.

items.note: 合肥、寿春之间的水道，魏吴淮南攻守多循此水。

e.note: The waterway between Hefei and Shouchun; Wei and Wu attacks and defences in Huainan mostly followed it.

items.note: 祁山即在西汉水北岸。

e.note: Mount Qi stands on the north bank of the Xihan River.

items.note: 沓中、阴平皆在白水流域，白水关扼其下游入蜀之口。

e.note: Tazhong and Yinping both lie in the Bai River basin, and Baishui Pass guards the point where its lower course leads into Shu.

items.note: 204 年曹操于淇水口下枋木成堰，遏淇水入白沟。

e.note: In 204 Cao Cao sank timber piles at the mouth of the Qi to build a weir, diverting the Qi into the Baigou Canal.

items.note: 69 年王景治河，同时整治汴渠，自荥阳东流经浚仪、睢阳至彭城入泗，是洛阳通往徐、扬的主要水道。官渡即在其上游。

e.mod: old course of the Bian River
e.note: In 69, while taming the Yellow River, Wang Jing also restored the Bian Canal, which ran east from Xingyang past Junyi and Suiyang to join the Si at Pengcheng. It was the main waterway from Luoyang to Xu and Yang provinces; Guandu lay on its upper course.

items.note: 战国魏所开鸿沟水系的主干，沟通河、淮。

e.mod: along the Jialu and Shaying rivers
e.note: The trunk of the Honggou canal system dug by the state of Wei in the Warring States period, linking the Yellow River and the Huai.

items.note: 春秋吴王夫差所开，沟通江淮。

e.note: Dug by Fuchai, King of Wu, in the Spring and Autumn period to link the Yangtze and the Huai.

items.note: 秦汉已有自吴通京口的水道，孙吴时为建业与吴会之间的漕路。

e.note: A waterway from Wu to Jingkou already existed in the Qin and Han; under Sun Wu it was the grain route between Jianye and Wu and Kuaiji.

items.note: 西汉武帝时所开，自长安引渭水东至华阴。

e.note: Dug under Emperor Wu of the Western Han, it led water from the Wei River east from Chang'an to Huayin.

items.note: 秦所开，沟通湘、漓二水。

e.note: Dug under the Qin to link the Xiang and Li rivers.

items.note: 关中与汉中的天然屏障，其间有子午、傥骆、褒斜、陈仓诸道。诸葛亮五次北伐都要翻越秦岭，粮运艰难是蜀汉北伐最大的掣肘。

e.note: The natural barrier between Guanzhong and Hanzhong, crossed by the Ziwu, Tangluo, Baoye and Chencang roads. All five of Zhuge Liang's northern campaigns had to cross the Qinling, and the difficulty of moving grain over them was the greatest constraint on Shu Han's campaigns.

items.note: 汉中与巴蜀之间的屏障，米仓道、金牛道穿越其间。

e.note: The barrier between Hanzhong and Ba–Shu, crossed by the Micang and Jinniu roads.

items.note: 河北与并州的分界。黄巾余部黑山军张燕盘踞其中，众号百万。

e.note: The divide between Hebei and Bing Province. Zhang Yan's Black Mountain army, a Yellow Turban remnant said to number a million, was based in these mountains.

items.note: 关中与陇右的分界，陇关、萧关扼其要道。

e.note: The divide between Guanzhong and Longyou, its main routes guarded by the Long and Xiao passes.

items.note: 91 年耿夔、任尚于此大破北单于。

e.note: In 91 Geng Kui and Ren Shang routed the Northern Chanyu here.

items.note: 89 年窦宪破北匈奴后登此山，班固作《封燕然山铭》。

e.note: In 89, after defeating the Northern Xiongnu, Dou Xian climbed this mountain, and Ban Gu wrote the Inscription for the Feng Sacrifice on Mount Yanran.

items.note: 南阳盆地北缘，鲁阳、叶县扼其东口。

e.note: The northern rim of the Nanyang Basin, its eastern outlets guarded by Luyang and She County.

items.note: 魏吴江淮之间的屏障，魏弋阳与吴蕲春隔山相望。

e.note: The barrier between Wei and Wu in the Jiang–Huai region; Wei's Yiyang and Wu's Qichun faced each other across the mountains.

items.note: 东汉 69 年哀牢国内附，以其地置永昌郡。

e.note: In 69 the Ailao kingdom submitted to the Eastern Han, which made its lands into Yongchang Commandery.

items.note: 洛阳北面的黄土岭，东汉帝陵不少在其上，有“生在苏杭，葬在北邙”之说；189 年董卓于北邙迎回少帝。

e.note: The loess ridge north of Luoyang, where many of the Eastern Han emperors were buried; there is a saying "Be born in Suzhou or Hangzhou, be buried at Beimang". In 189 Dong Zhuo met the Young Emperor at Beimang and brought him back.

items.note: 甘肃文县与四川青川、平武之间的山岭，阴平道越此南下。

e.note: The ridge between Wen County in Gansu and Qingchuan and Pingwu in Sichuan; the Yinping Road crossed it going south.

items.note: 沿斜水、褒水河谷开凿的栈道，长四百七十里，为关中通汉中的主道。诸葛亮 228 年扬言由此北出，234 年实由此出屯五丈原。

e.note: A plank road built along the valleys of the Ye and Bao rivers, 470 li long, the main route from Guanzhong to Hanzhong. In 228 Zhuge Liang announced that he would come north this way, and in 234 he actually did, camping at the Wuzhang Plains.

items.note: 长安正南出子午谷，经秦岭达汉中东部，路最近而最险。228 年魏延请率精兵五千由此奇袭长安，诸葛亮以为悬危未许；230 年曹真亦由此伐蜀，遇雨而还。

e.mod: south of Xi'an – east of Hanzhong, Shaanxi
e.note: It left Chang'an due south through the Ziwu Valley and crossed the Qinling to eastern Hanzhong: the shortest route and the most dangerous. In 228 Wei Yan asked to lead 5,000 picked troops this way to surprise Chang'an, but Zhuge Liang judged it too risky and refused; in 230 Cao Zhen also attacked Shu this way and turned back in the rain.

items.mod: 陕西宝鸡—凤县—略阳—勉县
items.note: 又称故道。出散关沿故道水南下，绕经武都东境至汉中，路远而平。215 年曹操征张鲁、228 年冬诸葛亮围陈仓皆经此道。

e.mod: Baoji – Feng County – Lüeyang – Mian County, Shaanxi
e.note: Also called the Gudao Road. It went out through San Pass and south along the Gudao River, curving through eastern Wudu to Hanzhong: long but level. Cao Cao's campaign against Zhang Lu in 215 and Zhuge Liang's siege of Chencang in winter 228 both went this way.

items.mod: 陕西勉县—甘肃礼县—天水
items.note: 自汉中西出，沿西汉水河谷北上至祁山，再出天水。道路较平缓、便于运粮，又可联络陇右羌氐，诸葛亮第一、四次北伐皆取此道。

e.mod: Mian County, Shaanxi – Li County – Tianshui, Gansu
e.note: It went west from Hanzhong and north up the Xihan River valley to Mount Qi, then out to Tianshui. The road was fairly gentle and easy for moving grain, and it allowed the army to link up with the Qiang and Di of Longyou; Zhuge Liang took it on his first and fourth northern campaigns.

items.mod: 陕西勉县—四川广元—剑阁—成都
items.note: 汉中经剑阁通成都的主道，相传秦惠王以石牛诈称能便金而开。263 年钟会大军沿此南下，受阻于剑阁。

e.mod: Mian County, Shaanxi – Guangyuan – Jiange – Chengdu, Sichuan
e.note: The main route from Hanzhong through Jiange to Chengdu; legend says it was opened when King Hui of Qin tricked Shu with stone oxen that supposedly dropped gold. In 263 Zhong Hui's army marched south along it and was stopped at Jiange.

items.note: 汉中越米仓山南下巴中的道路。215 年张鲁由此奔巴中，张郃随后南下宕渠，被张飞击退。

e.note: The route from Hanzhong over the Micang Mountains south to Bazhong. In 215 Zhang Lu fled this way to Bazhong; Zhang He later pushed south to Dangqu and was beaten back by Zhang Fei.

items.note: 207 年夏雨水泛滥、滨海道路不通，曹操用田畴之计出卢龙塞，循断绝二百年的古道，“堑山堙谷五百余里”，经白檀、平冈直趋柳城，乌桓猝不及防。

e.note: In summer 207 floods made the coast road impassable, so Cao Cao took Tian Chou's advice, went out through Lulong Fort and followed an old road disused for two hundred years, "cutting through mountains and filling valleys for more than 500 li", by way of Baitan and Pinggang straight to Liucheng, catching the Wuhuan off guard.

items.mod: 河南新安东（汉函谷关遗址）
items.note: 汉武帝时自弘农县东移至新安，为洛阳西面门户；故关在今灵宝。

e.mod: east of Xin'an, Henan (Han Hangu Pass site)
e.note: Under Emperor Wu of Han it was moved east from Hongnong to Xin'an, as the western gateway to Luoyang; the old pass is at today's Lingbao.

items.note: 关中东南门户，通南阳、荆襄。

e.note: The southeastern gateway of Guanzhong, leading to Nanyang and Jing–Xiang.

items.note: 陈仓道（故道）北口。215 年曹操由此征张鲁，228 年冬诸葛亮由此出围陈仓。

e.note: Northern entrance of the Chencang Road (Gudao Road). Cao Cao went this way against Zhang Lu in 215, and Zhuge Liang came out this way to besiege Chencang in winter 228.

items.note: 陇山东麓关口，关中通陇右的要道。

e.note: The pass at the eastern foot of the Long Mountains, on the main road from Guanzhong to Longyou.

items.note: 关中通往安定、北地的门户。

e.note: The gateway from Guanzhong to Anding and Beidi.

items.mod: 陕西勉县西（汉代阳平关）
items.note: 汉中西面门户，又称阳安关。215 年曹操于此破张卫，217—219 年刘备与夏侯渊相持于此，263 年钟会遣胡烈攻破此关。

e.mod: west of Mian County, Shaanxi (the Han-era Yangping Pass)
e.note: The western gateway of Hanzhong, also called Yang'an Pass. Cao Cao broke Zhang Wei here in 215, Liu Bei faced Xiahou Yuan here from 217 to 219, and in 263 Zhong Hui sent Hu Lie to take the pass.

items.mod: 四川青川东北（地望有争议）
items.note: 益州北面要隘，刘璋使杨怀、高沛守之；212 年刘备斩二将夺关南下。

e.note: The key pass on the northern edge of Yi Province, held for Liu Zhang by Yang Huai and Gao Pei; in 212 Liu Bei beheaded the two commanders, took the pass and marched south.

items.note: 西汉水北岸孤峰，扼陇右通汉中的要道。诸葛亮第一、四次北伐皆出祁山，演义附会为“六出祁山”。

e.mod: east of Li County, Gansu (Qishan Fort)
e.note: A lone peak on the north bank of the Xihan River, guarding the main route from Longyou to Hanzhong. Zhuge Liang came out by Mount Qi on his first and fourth northern campaigns; the Romance stretches this into "six sorties from Mount Qi".

items.note: 即成皋关，洛阳东面门户，其西旋门关为汉末洛阳八关之一。演义“三英战吕布”安排在此，正史中讨董联军并未在此与吕布交战。

e.note: That is, Chenggao Pass, the eastern gateway of Luoyang; Xuanmen Pass to its west was one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han. The Romance sets "the three heroes fight Lü Bu" here, but in the histories the coalition against Dong Zhuo never fought Lü Bu here.

items.note: 洛阳南面门户，汉末八关之一。

e.note: The southern gateway of Luoyang, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han.

items.note: 洛阳东南经嵩山通颍川的要道，汉末八关之一。

e.mod: southeast of Yanshi District, Luoyang, Henan
e.note: The route southeast from Luoyang past Mount Songgao to Yingchuan, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han.

items.note: 洛阳北面黄河渡口，含小平津，汉末八关之一。189 年张让等劫少帝出逃至此，投河自尽。

e.mod: northeast of Mengjin District, Luoyang, Henan
e.note: The Yellow River crossing north of Luoyang, including Xiaoping Ford, one of the Eight Passes of Luoyang in the late Han. In 189 Zhang Rang and the other eunuchs abducted the Young Emperor and fled here, then drowned themselves in the river.

items.note: 太行山陉道西口，上党东面门户。206 年高幹据此拒曹。

e.note: The western end of a defile through the Taihang Mountains and the eastern gateway of Shangdang. In 206 Gao Gan held it against Cao Cao.

items.mod: 河北石家庄鹿泉区西（土门关）
items.note: 太行八陉之一，河北通并州的要道。

e.mod: west of Luquan District, Shijiazhuang, Hebei (Tumen Pass)
e.note: One of the Eight Defiles of the Taihang, the main route from Hebei to Bing Province.

items.mod: 山西代县西北（雁门关一带）
items.note: 并州北门，又称西陉。

e.mod: northwest of Dai County, Shanxi (Yanmen Pass area)
e.note: The northern gate of Bing Province, also called the Western Defile.

items.note: 燕山西段要隘。

e.note: A key pass in the western Yan Mountains.

items.mod: 河北迁西北（喜峰口一带）
items.note: 燕山东段关隘，经此可出塞直趋柳城。207 年曹操用田畴之计由此奇袭乌桓。

e.note: A pass in the eastern Yan Mountains, from which one could go beyond the frontier straight to Liucheng. In 207 Cao Cao followed Tian Chou's plan and made his surprise attack on the Wuhuan this way.

items.mod: 甘肃敦煌西北（小方盘城）
items.note: 汉代通西域北道的关口。

e.note: The Han pass on the Northern Route of the Western Regions.

items.note: 汉代通西域南道的关口。

e.note: The Han pass on the Southern Route of the Western Regions.

items.note: 长江出三峡后的门户，荆门山在南岸、虎牙山在北岸。吴于此横江设铁锁，280 年被王濬烧断。

e.note: The gateway of the Yangtze as it leaves the Three Gorges, with Mount Jingmen on the south bank and Mount Huya on the north. Wu stretched iron chains across the river here, which Wang Jun burned through in 280.
